collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Missed calls go to voicemail while on jobs, Callers often move on to competitor instead of leaving a message, Calls mostly roll to voicemail, Wife sometimes helps answer but both are busy
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: Can’t answer every call; accepts missed calls as part of the job while busy on jobs.

transcript:
User: Yeah, I got a voicemail from you people. This better be quick, I've got three jobs waiting.
Agent: Totally—I'll keep it quick. What caught your attention in the voicemail?
User: My wife made me call. Something about saving money, but I'm not buying it. Is this a scam?
Agent: No, it’s not a scam—I get why you’d ask. When you say “saving money,” what’s the situation you’re worried is costing you right now—missed calls going to voicemail, or something else?
User: Everyone says they can save me money. Why do you need to know about my situation? Sounds fishy.
Agent: Fair question—it’s only so I don’t waste your time or pitch the wrong thing. Are you mainly trying to stop missed calls turning into lost jobs, or is it a different cost you’re focused on?
User: That's none of your business. I know what I'm doing. Just tell me how you supposedly save me money.
Agent: Got it—you don’t need to share anything. We save you money by catching and converting the calls you miss (busy on a job, after-hours, or short-staffed): we answer, screen, and book the job or take a message so you don’t lose that work to the next contractor.  

Is your biggest leak right now missed inbound calls, yes or no?
User: I handle my calls just fine. Your service sounds like something I don't need. What's the catch?
Agent: No catch—if you’re not missing calls, it probably isn’t worth paying for. Before we drop it, do you ever have calls hit voicemail when you’re on a ladder, driving, or after-hours?
User: Of course, but that's part of the job. I can't answer every call, and that's how it is.
Agent: Right—when you’re on a job, you can’t stop and grab every call. When those calls hit voicemail, do they usually leave a message, or do they just move on to the next guy?
User: They sometimes leave messages, but most move on. But that's none of your concern, really.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—people are impatient. Roughly how many calls a week do you think hit voicemail?
User: I'm not giving out numbers. Why do you even need to know that? Feels like prying.
Agent: Totally fair—I’m not looking for exact numbers. I only ask because if it’s just the occasional missed call, it’s probably not worth your time, but if it’s frequent and people move on, that’s where the “saving money” comes from.  

Would you say it’s rare, or does it happen pretty often?
User: I don't really keep track. But again, why do you need to know this? Feels unnecessary.
Agent: You’re right to push on that—I’m only trying to figure out if there’s anything to fix, because if you’re missing calls and most move on, that’s exactly where the money leaks.  

When a call comes in and you’re tied up, is there anyone (your wife, an office line, answering service) who can pick it up, or does it just roll to voicemail?
User: It mostly rolls to voicemail. My wife sometimes helps, but we're both busy. What's your point?
Agent: My point is: if it’s rolling to voicemail and most callers move on, you’re losing jobs you never even get a chance to quote. Would you want those missed callers to get answered and booked automatically while you’re working, or would you rather leave it as-is?
User: I don't need someone else managing my calls. I've done fine for years. Goodbye.
Agent: Totally hear you—if you’ve been fine for years, no need to change anything. Thanks for taking the minute, and hope those jobs go smoothly today.
